news.title: Dividend of ₹2.10 announced
news.body: Dividend of ₹2.10 is the same as last year. Ex-date: 19th June 2026 Payment date: 15th August 2026 Dividend yield will be 0.3%, which is about the same as the industry average. Sustainability & Growth Dividend is well covered by both earnings (24% earnings payout ratio) and cash flows (2% cash payout ratio). The dividend has increased by an average of 5.6% per year over the past 8 years. However, payments have been volatile during that time. EPS is expected to grow by 41% over the next 3 years, which should provide support to the dividend and adequate earnings cover.

news.title: Full year 2026 earnings: EPS and revenues miss analyst expectations
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹8.87 (up from ₹8.42 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹998.6b (up 2.7% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹19.1b (up 5.6% from FY 2025). Profit margin: 1.9% (in line with FY 2025). Revenue missed analyst estimates by 13%. Earnings per share (EPS) also missed analyst estimates by 4.8%. Revenue is forecast to grow 15% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 11% growth forecast for the Insurance industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has increased by 11% per year whereas the company’s share price has increased by 6% per year.

news.title: HDFC Life Insurance Company Limited announced that it expects to receive INR 9.999999759 billion in funding from HDFC Bank Limited
news.body: HDFC Life Insurance Company Limited announced that it will issue 14,523,906 equity shares at a price of INR 688.52 for total gross proceeds not exceeding INR 9,999,999,759.12 on April 16, 2026. The transaction will include participation from its parent, HDFC Bank Limited, that currently holds 50.21% stake of the company. The stake of HDFC Bank Limited in the company will increase to 50.54% post the transaction. The transaction has been approved by the board of directors of the company. The transaction is subject to approval of the shareholders and other regulatory / statutory approvals as may be necessary. The company will issue securities on preferential basis.

news.title: New minor risk - Dividend sustainability
news.body: The company has an unstable dividend paying track record. The dividend has had an annual drop of over 20% in the past. Dividend yield: 0.3% This is considered a minor risk. If the company has cut or reduced its dividend in the past, it may be a sign that the underlying business is too cyclical to consistently maintain or grow the dividend over the long-term. It may also indicate the company prioritizes other outcomes instead of maintaining the dividend. For dividend paying companies, any reduction in the dividend can significantly impact the share price. This is currently the only risk that has been identified for the company.
